text:
Sam L: opening thread for an escalated customer bug — ACME reported dozens of 401s after users completed SSO + MFA. Happens sporadically across web and mobile webview.

Anya R: can you paste a minimal repro and the error body? we need headers + cookie bits.

Sam L: repro steps from user (clean session):
1) user clicks 'Sign in with Okta' on acme.app (top-level).
2) Okta redirects back to our /auth/callback which then does device-trust rekey and redirects to /app.
3) Some users see immediate 401 on subsequent API calls from the app shell (~2–10s). Others are fine. Happens more on iOS Safari + embedded iOS WKWebView.

Sam L: example curl of failing API (token derived from cookie session):
```
curl -i -X GET "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/usage" \
  -H "Cookie: rw_session=eyJhbGciOi..."
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":"invalid_session","message":"session not found"}
```

Sam L: here's the auth callback response headers captured from the browser devtools (redacted):
```
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Location: https://acme.app/app
Set-Cookie: rw_session=eyJhbGciOi...; Domain=.acme.app; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; Max-Age=120
Set-Cookie: device_jwt=abc123; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=None; Max-Age=3600
```

Anya R: interesting — session cookie lacks SameSite attribute. on top-level flows that should be OK, but in some webviews the redirect is treated as third-party and older versions block cookies unless SameSite=None. also rw_session Max-Age is very short (120s) — could be race with rekey.

Devon K: also seeing device_jwt rotation logs that re-issue a new jwt at the end of the callback. if a frontend immediately exchanges device_jwt for a bearer token while the cookie rekey runs async, there might be a mismatch where the cookie points to a different session id than the token.

Kevin P: can you paste the rekey flow snippet from logs? I want to see timing.

Sam L: logs (times intentionally rounded):
```
[10:22:14] POST /auth/callback (okta) -> start rekey job
[10:22:14.2] rekey: invalidate old device_jwt (id x123)
[10:22:14.4] rekey: create new rw_session -> id s789 (Set-Cookie header sent)
[10:22:15.0] frontend: exchange device_jwt x123 for api token -> success
[10:22:15.1] API: token introspect -> token valid but session lookup by cookie id s789 fails (session not found)
[10:22:16] rekey: cleanup old session index entry
```

Sam L: so a small window where token and cookie disagree. frontend obtains a token tied to the old device_jwt while the cookie has been rotated to a new session id. subsequent API calls rely on cookie-backed session lookup and get 401.

Maya C: this seems like a rotate-on-login race — we rotate the cookie/session synchronously but the token exchange path still accepts the pre-rotation device_jwt. mobile webviews amplify timing variance.

Anya R: repro on our side? which customers' OS/browser versions most affected?

Sam L: mostly iOS 15–16 Safari + a couple of Android webviews (older Chromium). Desktop Chrome rare. ACME reports ~18% of logins hit the window.

Devon K: low-effort mitigation: make rekey fully idempotent for a short grace window — accept recently-rotated device_jwt values for 30–60s, or delay invalidation of the old device_jwt until after token exchange completes.

eng-security: tagging — this affects session consistency and could be exploited for DoS of session creation if not rate-limited. review needed.

Kevin P: quick patch suggestion: when issuing new rw_session cookie, include SameSite=None; Secure so webviews accept cookies; increase rw_session Max-Age to 300s; and add a short grace period where both old and new device_jwt map to the same session id for 45s.

Sam L: ok deploying a fix candidate to staging now (will run with additional logging).

sre-bot: deploy triggered by Sam L — staging/service-auth v2026.03.15-rc1 at 1704509950

Sam L: staging results — login flow on iOS webview shows no 401s across 200 tries. added extra logging confirms overlap window closed after 45s grace.

Maya C: need to confirm no security regression (old tokens accepted too long). eng-security: please review token grace logic.

eng-security: looked at the patch. acceptable for 45s grace given short-lived device_jwt and extra rate limits. recommend telemetry flag enabled for 48h and postmortem.

Anya R: rolling to prod in a phased canary: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 2 hours, will monitor 401 rate and session churn.

Sam L: prod canary started. will update when 401s drop for ACME.

Sam L: update 30m later — ACME reporting successful logins, 401s dropped from ~18% -> 0.8% during canary window. proceeding to 100%. :tada:

Sam L: resolution notes for support doc: root cause = session/cookie rotation race during SSO+MFA rekey; contributing factors = short cookie TTL + webview SameSite handling. fix = add SameSite=None; extend session TTL to 300s; add 45s grace window for device_jwt mapping and telemetry.

Anya R: thanks team. creating KB entry and escalating to docs for a note about webview quirks + recommended IdP redirect patterns.

Sam L: closing thread, will attach KB link once up.
